SRU Manual
Access via IndCat SRU
Access via IndCat SRU
The INFLIBNET IndCat union catalogue is accessible via the
                            Search/Retrieve via URL (SRU) interface.
SRU is an internationally recognised, standardised web-based protocol
                            that facilitates bibliographic discovery. Users and applications can
                            query the catalogue using the Contextual Query Language (CQL),
                            supporting searches through a combination of indexes, terms and
                            Boolean operators.
Requests are delivered in a structured XML format, enabling library
                            systems, discovery tools and developers to retrieve and reuse
                            bibliographic data seamlessly.
The SRU standard is published and maintained by the Library of
                            Congress and its full specification is available at:
http://www.loc.gov/standards/sru/
IndCat-GEN
This profile is openly available for general use and does not require
                            authentication. It covers the most commonly used bibliographic fields
                            and grants access to the complete set of bibliographic records in
                            IndCat Books.
Recommended for end-user applications such as reference management
                            and bibliographic citation tools.

The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2026
Understanding and addressing the high cost of a healthy diet
2026
Also available in:
Arabic
Chinese
French
Russian
Spanish
Despite sustained, gradual improvement in recent years, global hunger and food insecurity remain far above the targets set by the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. It is estimated that 645 million people faced hunger in 2025.  Beyond ensuring access to sufficient dietary energy, populations must have economic access to safe, diverse and nutritious foods. Yet, healthy diets are unaffordable for about 2.7 billion people worldwide, with the crisis deepening particularly in Africa. The 2026 edition of The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World evaluates this pressing challenge, exploring the structural drivers behind the persistently high cost of a healthy diet. This report reveals that the high prices of nutrient-dense items – specifically animal source foods, fruits and vegetables – account for nearly 70 percent of the cost of a healthy diet. By leveraging existing data and analytical tools, it examines how geographical disparities, agricultural productivity deficits, and value chain inefficiencies, including food loss and waste, create formidable barriers to accessing a healthy diet. To sustainably achieve Zero Hunger, policymakers must implement targeted, multisectoral interventions, from shifting agricultural subsidies towards horticulture, to investing in robust cold chains and transport networks. This report provides a comprehensive strategy for governments and stakeholders aiming to structurally lower diet costs and safeguard human capital, while avoiding the hidden costs of agrifood systems.

Restoration progress report: Nature's comeback
Scaling ecosystem restoration for people and planet
2026
Also available in:
No results found.
At the midpoint of the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration, this report provides the first comprehensive global assessment of progress towards restoring degraded ecosystems and achieving international restoration targets and commitments. Drawing on data from national reporting to the Rio Conventions and other multilateral environmental agreements, as well as global restoration monitoring initiatives and other sources, it evaluates the extent to which restoration efforts are contributing to the goals of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, with a particular focus on Target 2.Covering terrestrial, freshwater, marine and coastal ecosystems, the report examines restoration achievements to date, the scale and drivers of ecosystem degradation, documented restoration efforts, and the financing supporting implementation. It assesses whether current progress is sufficient to meet global ambitions and identifies key gaps in monitoring, implementation, policy and investment that continue to constrain action.Recognizing that restoration success depends on more than the number of hectares restored, the report also considers the social, institutional and governance dimensions that underpin lasting outcomes. Secure tenure rights, gender equality, meaningful participation, and the knowledge, rights and leadership of Indigenous Peoples are highlighted as essential components of effective and equitable restoration.Structured around two central questions, the report asks: How much progress has been made towards restoring degraded ecosystems, and what actions are needed to accelerate restoration at scale? It concludes by identifying practical solutions and strategic pathways to close existing gaps, strengthen implementation and turn restoration commitments into measurable results. As monitoring systems continue to evolve, future assessments will provide an increasingly robust picture of global progress towards ecosystem recovery by 2030 and beyond.

The State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture 2026
Blue Transformation: turning vision into impact
2026
Also available in:
Arabic
Chinese
French
Russian
Spanish
The State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture 2026 provides the latest evidence-based information and insights on challenges, opportunities and solutions shaping the present and future of the sector. This 2026 edition showcases how FAO is translating the Blue Transformation vision into impact, deploying field projects in close collaboration with Members, partners and key stakeholders. It highlights efforts to maximize the contribution of aquatic foods to global food security, poverty alleviation and economic development, enhancing policy advocacy, advancing scientific research and innovations, and furthering capacity development.Part 1 presents an up-to-date global review of fisheries and aquaculture production, employment, utilization and trade, benefiting from significant improvements in data collection and in analytical and assessment tools and methodologies. Part 2 explores the transformational actions being undertaken by FAO, its Members and key stakeholders to catalyse the changes required to support aquaculture expansion and intensification, effective management of global fisheries, and upgrading of aquatic value chains. Part 3 covers FAO commitments to strengthen aquatic food systems in a holistic manner, with a focus on the role of regional fishery bodies in translating international commitments into actionable regional measures; it emphasizes the importance of global climate research and models to inform adaptive fisheries management policies and decisions. It also presents an outlook on future trends for fisheries and aquaculture development up to 2034 based on projections.The State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture is aimed at a wide and expanding audience of policymakers, managers, researchers, private actors, civil society activists and consumers.

General principles of food hygiene
2023
Also available in:
French
Spanish
This document outlines the general principles that should be understood and followed by food business operators at all stages of the food chain and that provide a basis for competent authorities to oversee food safety and suitability.This edition contains a new annex which introduces tools to determine the critical control points in a hazard analysis and critical control point (HACCP) system.The term "Codex Alimentarius" is Latin and means "food code”. Codex standards are international food texts, i.e. standards, codes of practice, codes of hygienic practice, guidelines and other recommendations, established to protect the health of the consumers and to ensure fair practices in the food trade. The collection of food standards and related texts adopted by the Codex Alimentarius Commission is known as the Codex Alimentarius.

Technical study
Making locally led adaptation work for women farmers
Evidence, financing models and enabling pathways
2026
Also available in:
No results found.
Climate change is already reshaping agrifood systems, and its impacts are not felt equally: women make up 42 percent of the agrifood workforce, yet face persistent gaps in access to land, credit, technology and decision-making. At the same time, women farmers are already adapting. Locally led adaptation has become a growing focus of climate policy and finance, but locally led is not automatically women-led, and evidence on how it works in agrifood systems, and on how women farmers lead it, remains limited. This publication gathers insights from 34 FAO-supported initiatives in 26 countries on how adaptation support can shift decision-making and resources towards women. Most were not designed under the locally led adaptation label; considered side by side, they show which types of support, and which combinations of them, make a difference. The publication focuses on three dimensions – organizational arrangements, knowledge and learning processes, and financing models – and identifies 12 support mechanisms that increase women farmers’ influence over climate adaptation decisions and resources. It is offered as a starting point towards a systemic strategy for locally led adaptation in agrifood systems, one that can help shift adaptation from projects that include women to adaptation that women lead.

Report of the  Thirteenth session of the South West Indian Ocean Fisheries Commission, Moroni, Comoros, 22–24 January 2026 / Rapport de la treizième session de la Commission des pêches pour le sud-ouest de l’océan Indien, Moroni, Comores, 22-24 janvier 2026
2026
Also available in:
No results found.
The Thirteenth Session of the South West Indian Ocean Fisheries Commission (SWIOFC), held in Moroni, Comoros, from 22 to 24 January 2026, brought together representatives of all twelve Member States and regional and international partners to review progress and advance regional fisheries cooperation. The Session endorsed key scientific and technical recommendations and adopted the 2026 Programme of Work, reaffirming the Commission’s commitment to sustainable fisheries management through strengthened scientific capacity, harmonized data systems, improved stock assessments, enhanced regional collaboration, and effective implementation of the Minimum Terms and Conditions (MTC) Guidelines.
La treizième session de la Commission des pêches pour le sud-ouest de l’océan Indien, tenue à Moroni, aux Comores, du 22 au 24 janvier 2026, a réuni des représentants des douze États membres ainsi que des partenaires régionaux et internationaux afin d’examiner les progrès accomplis et de renforcer la coopération régionale dans le domaine des pêches. La session a approuvé des recommandations scientifiques et techniques clés et adopté le Programme de travail 2026, réaffirmant l’engagement de la Commission en faveur d’une gestion durable des pêches, grâce au renforcement des capacités scientifiques, à l’harmonisation des systèmes de données, à l’amélioration des évaluations des stocks, au renforcement de la coopération régionale et à la mise en œuvre effective des Directives relatives aux conditions minimales.
Manual / guide
From field to airwaves
A rural radio practitioner’s guide
2026
Also available in:
No results found.
This guide shows how a participatory communication approach can turn radio into a tool owned by rural communities. It walks readers through the full process of designing, producing and sharing programmes and other communication outputs, from identifying priority issues and co-creating content to broadcasting, dissemination and evaluation, with farmers and their organizations at the centre of every stage. It is intended for extension workers, farmer field school facilitators and members, focal points of producer organizations, development practitioners and radio professionals who want to work together to drive positive change. Combined with mobile phones and digital platforms, participatory radio becomes a powerful means of bringing together diverse actors to discuss and tackle the main challenges facing rural communities, and of ensuring that their voices are heard.
Technical brief
Bien connaître son secteur
Dossier d’investissement sur l’amélioration des données relatives au secteur de l’élevage de tilapia au Zimbabwe
2026
Also available in:
English
Une enquête cadre conduite par FISH4ACP a révélé que le secteur de l’élevage de tilapia au Zimbabwe était bien plus important qu’on ne le pensait auparavant, comptant 8 000 pisciculteurs. Ces résultats sont en train de redéfinir la manière dont le gouvernement, les bailleurs de fonds et les banques planifient leur action dans ce secteur en pleine expansion. Cette enquête devrait générer un rapport avantages-coûts de 5,9 et un rendement de 116 pour cent sur cinq ans, en permettant de cibler les subventions, les services de vulgarisation et les mesures de biosécurité là où ils sont le plus utiles. Elle influence aussi la planification nationale en matière de sécurité alimentaire. Les enquêtes cadres ne génèrent pas de rendements directs, mais elles doivent être considérées comme des investissements publics à haut rendement dans le domaine de l’information et de l’intelligence économique. Consultez le dossier d'investissement complet pour en savoir plus et comprendre comment les enquêtes-cadres pourraient avoir un impact dans d’autres régions.
Technical brief
Agrifood systems in nationally determined contributions: a global analysis
Synthesis Report 2026
2026
Also available in:
No results found.
Agrifood systems are central to both climate action and food security, yet they face growing risks from climate change while contributing significantly to global greenhouse gas emissions. Drawing on a global analysis of the third round of nationally determined contributions (NDCs), this technical brief examines how countries are integrating agrifood systems into their climate mitigation and adaptation commitments under the Paris Agreement. It highlights key trends in priorities and ambition, identifies opportunities and challenges for implementation, and assesses the extent to which NDCs address financing, capacity-building and readiness needs. It also explores how countries are incorporating elements of a just transition to support climate-resilient, inclusive and sustainable agrifood systems. Prepared for the UNFCC COP31, it aims to inform decision-makers, negotiators and development partners on the actions and enabling conditions needed to translate commitments into effective implementation.

Catalogue of mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex and their association with drug resistance:  web annex C: simplified graded mutation list, 3rd ed.
World Health Organization (Publication Date: 2026-11-03, Accepted: 2026-11-03, Available Online: 2026-11-03)
Show more
This web annex accompanies the third edition of the *Catalogue of mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex and their association with drug resistance*, which provides a standardized reference for interpreting genetic mutations associated with phenotypic resistance to antituberculosis medicines.

The annex presents a simplified version of the Graded Mutation List provided in Web Annex B, summarizing the evidence supporting the classification of genetic variants according to their association with drug resistance. For each mutation, it provides phenotypic drug-susceptibility data, statistical measures of genotype–phenotype association, initial and final confidence classifications, supporting datasets, and supplementary grading considerations. It also identifies changes in mutation classifications compared with the second edition of the catalogue. The simplified list prioritizes WHO-derived data when the initial confidence grading is supported exclusively by the WHO dataset and otherwise presents results from the broader dataset. As specified in the main report, the list must be used alongside additional grading rules and interpretation criteria within an automated, quality-assured sequencing analysis framework.

WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 3: diagnosis: web annex C: tests for TB infection: TBSTs; TSTs; IGRAs: list of studies included in systematic review, GRADE profiles, evidence to decision tables, systematic reviews, 2nd ed.
World Health Organization (Publication Date: 2026-11-03, Accepted: 2026-11-03, Available Online: 2026-11-03)
Show more
This web annex provides the supporting evidence for the recommendations on tuberculosis (TB) infection testing in the second edition of the WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, Module 3: Diagnosis. It presents systematic reviews, lists of included studies, GRADE evidence profiles and evidence-to-decision tables assessing Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigen-based skin tests (TBSTs), tuberculin skin tests (TSTs) and interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs). 

The evidence examines diagnostic accuracy, comparative test performance, concordance and safety, including sensitivity, specificity and the certainty of available findings. Assessments cover populations at increased risk of TB infection and specific groups, including children, people vaccinated with bacille Calmette–Guérin (BCG) and people living with HIV. Comparisons between TBSTs and established testing methods consider their potential role in identifying individuals who may benefit from TB preventive treatment, alongside issues of test availability, affordability, feasibility and equity. The annex documents the evidence and judgements underpinning guideline development, including limitations arising from study design, risk of bias, inconsistency and imprecision.

Catalogue of mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex and their association with drug resistance: web annex B: graded mutation list and accompanying catalogue data/resources, 3rd ed.
World Health Organization (Publication Date: 2026-11-03, Accepted: 2026-11-03, Available Online: 2026-11-03)
Show more
This web annex accompanies the third edition of the *Catalogue of mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex and their association with drug resistance*, which provides a standardized reference for interpreting genetic mutations associated with phenotypic resistance to antituberculosis medicines.

The annex presents the Graded Mutation List and accompanying datasets supporting the interpretation of genomic drug resistance. It provides classifications of genetic variants according to their association with resistance, together with supporting genotype–phenotype statistics, information on mutation frequencies across *Mycobacterium tuberculosis* complex lineages, and comparisons with the previous edition of the catalogue. Additional worksheets include mutations not assigned a confidence grade, definitions of the terms and variables used, genomic coordinates of resistance-associated genes, and detailed catalogue statistics. The Graded Mutation List is intended to be used alongside the additional grading rules and interpretation criteria described in the main report, preferably within validated, quality-assured bioinformatics workflows that integrate these components for sample-level resistance interpretation.
